notes: Settings of the exploratory whole-sky sweep (STL-009). Cuts, feature policy, pass marks and the cross-match window come from the UC-01 predeclaration; these are the sweep's own. Three HDBSCAN grid points give each candidate a stability; one null field per tile gives the false-positive rate. The sweep clusters with fast_hdbscan's Boruvka HDBSCAN, which matches scikit-learn's labels on the fixtures but grows about n log n rather than n squared with the stars in a tile (#133); the predeclared UC-01 run keeps sklearn-hdbscan. The CMD coherence check places every member at the cluster's distance (cmd_policy cluster-distance, STL-010), so a member's own parallax error does not blur the sequence. Each candidate also gets a significance in sigma (STL-011, after Hunt & Reffert 2021): its members' 10th-nearest-neighbour distances in the feature space against those of the 5x as many (at least 50) non-members around it; below 3 sigma it is rejected, and a potentially new one must beat every false candidate its tile's null fields produced. The sky is swept once per distance scale (STL-012): 12-degree tiles with a 3-degree rim within 250 pc (parallax 4 mas and up), 4-degree tiles within 1 kpc and 2-degree tiles beyond, each shell searched over its parallax range widened by 15% so a cluster on a boundary is seen whole; tile_deg stays the prepared catalogue's band size. A tile with more stars than max_tile_stars after the cuts is skipped with that reason rather than searched. Every grid point is capped at the largest cluster the field-fraction check accepts (max_cluster_size, #159): inside a shell's parallax window the field piles up at the window's dense edge, and uncapped, excess-of-mass selection kept that field-sized group instead of the real clusters inside it.
